summary: Wallace Harbour Sector Light, Nova Scotia: the front of an 1904 range pair that led ships into Wallace Harbour; a sector light since 1990, now owned by a local association.

structures.note: Lighthouse Directory 8.5 m (28 ft); SaltWire 8 m (26 ft); the 1904 report gives 30 feet to the lantern ventilator.

access.note: Beside Route 6 on the east side of the harbour; no parking provided (Lighthouse Directory). Grounds open, tower closed (Lighthouse Friends, Directory).

facts.agency: Wallace Area Development Association (owner); Canadian Coast Guard (operates the light)

events.note: Earlier lighthouse on Mullins Point, northeast of Palmer Point, marks the harbour, with a companion rear light soon after (Lighthouse Friends). Not this station; the earlier pair.
Macfarlane Point range lights (front and back) put in operation 20 October 1904; fixed red catoptric lights.
George Boyle appointed first keeper, 24 May 1905, $150 a year.
Lights electrified in 1958, after Noble Jamieson (keeper from 1940) was the final keeper.
Several vessels ran aground at the harbour, prompting the 1986 petition about foliage at the rear range light.
Converted to a sector light; lantern room replaced with a larger rectangular one; seaward markings changed from a vertical red stripe to two horizontal red stripes.
Rear range tower sold in March 1994 and moved in pieces to Malagash Point in 1995 (Lighthouse Friends, Lighthouse Directory). The rear tower, not this station.
Declared a heritage lighthouse in February 2015 under the Heritage Lighthouse Protection Act of 2008.
Wallace Area Development Association bought the lighthouse from the federal government in December 2015 for one dollar, with a $10,000 grant.

notes_for_editor: Owner conflict: Lighthouse Friends' page still says the Canadian Coast Guard owns the light (its 'owned by' line); SaltWire and the Lighthouse Directory say the Wallace Area Development Association has owned it since December 2015, and the story follows them. Rear-range removal dates disagree: SaltWire says the rear was taken apart in 1990 when the front became a sector light; Lighthouse Friends and the Directory say sold 1994 and moved 1995 (story follows these). A third site (novascotiavacation.ca) was read but not used: it gives 1988 and unsourced details. Heights: 8.5 m (28 ft) Directory; 8 m (26 ft) SaltWire and the record; 8.1 in the Coast Guard list (column unlabelled); 30 feet to the lantern ventilator in the 1904 report. Focal height: 12.4 m Coast Guard, 12.5 m (41 ft) Directory and 1904 report. Range: 21 nautical miles in the Coast Guard list (column read without its heading). The Mullins Point rear light: Lighthouse Friends dates an 1873 light and rear; the Lighthouse Directory dates the Mullins Point range rear to 1894; unresolved. Keepers: Boyle is confirmed by the 1905 statement; the names and dates of Lawson, Langille and Jamieson rest on Lighthouse Friends. Two OCR entries (D. Lawson in the 1914 statement and Robert Langville in the 1915 appointments table) were not matched to this station by position. The Marine corpus ends in 1924, so nothing checks Jamieson. The rear tower's buyer is a private person named in Lighthouse Friends; the story does not name him. The record's coordinates (45.813265, -63.462149) agree with Coast Guard entry 924 (45 48 46.8 N, 063 27 43.6 W) to about 20 m, so no position correction is proposed. The record's characteristic 'F R' is incomplete (sector light); see corrections. The review in docs/sources/review_2026-10-ca.md flagged the Wallace Harbour pair for a wrong position in one source; the front tower's position agrees across the record, the Coast Guard and Lighthouse Friends, so the flag probably concerns the rear half. No 1985 grounding was searched in newspapers (not searched for lack of budget and of a clear wreck record). No new photographs checked. Fact-check 2026-10-27: the story now states the owner disagreement (Lighthouse Friends' stale footer line against its own account of the December 2015 purchase) and the rear-tower disagreement (SaltWire's 1990 date against 1994 and 1995). The 1990 conversion cites the Directory, not the Coast Guard list, which has no conversion date. The 1904 report is dated by its own fiscal year (ended 30 June 1904), but the report records the 20 October 1904 operation date, after that year-end; the story reports the report's words and does not reconcile the two.
